Emergency Shutdown vs Normal Shutdown

An emergency shutdown is an automatic, fail safe action that drives the plant to a safe state when a hazardous condition is detected, without waiting for an operator. A normal shutdown is a planned, controlled sequence run by operators through the basic process control system. Both stop the process, but the purpose, speed and system used are very different.

PointEmergency shutdownNormal shutdown
TriggerTrip on a hazardous condition, fire and gas detection or manual ESD push buttonPlanned maintenance, low demand or operator decision
SystemIndependent safety instrumented system under IEC 61511Basic process control system
SpeedSeconds, valves move straight to the safe positionGradual ramp down over minutes or hours
Valve actionFail safe shutdown valves close, blowdown valves openControl valves throttled in sequence
RestartReset only after the cause is found and clearedNormal start up procedure
Design basisSafety integrity level and PFDavgProduction and equipment care

Because an emergency shutdown must work even when power, air or signal is lost, every element is designed to de energise to trip. A normal shutdown, by contrast, relies on the control system staying healthy throughout. Keeping the two separate is what prevents a single control failure from defeating the safety layer.
